waive.TypeOK: Shape check only: no behaviour change breaks it without also breaking a property above it.

mutations.name: no-takeover-guard
mutations.why: Two waiters that both judged the planted lock dead both remove and remake it: the second removes the first's new lock.

mutations.name: no-rejudge-inside-guard
mutations.why: takeOver acting on the main loop's judgement: a waiter that saw the dead lock gets the guard after another has already taken over, and removes that holder's lock.
mutations.search: /\ gown' = p /\ UNCHANGED gstalled /\ ctx' = [ctx EXCEPT ![p] = "tk"] /\ Goto(p, "j_owner")
mutations.replace: /\ gown' = p /\ UNCHANGED gstalled /\ ctx' = [ctx EXCEPT ![p] = "tk"] /\ Goto(p, "j_decide")

mutations.name: plain-acquire-skips-guard
mutations.why: Plain acquire without the guard: a process between mkdir and its owner write (asleep) leaves a half-made folder that looks abandoned; a takeover removes and remakes it, and the waking process writes its owner into the new lock: two holders.
mutations.search: /\ gown' = p /\ UNCHANGED gstalled /\ ctx' = [ctx EXCEPT ![p] = "ac"] /\ Goto(p, "acq_mkdir")

mutations.name: remote-release-skips-guard
mutations.why: The release of a holder on another computer without the guard: a takeover that judged its lock stale deletes after that holder woke and released and another waiter made a fresh lock, removing that waiter's lock.

mutations.name: local-release-skips-guard
mutations.why: The release of a holder on this computer without the guard.
mutations.equivalent: A live holder on this computer is never judged abandoned (only its dead pid condemns it, and a dead process does not release), so no takeover can land between its ownership check and its delete: the model finds the guard on a release necessary only through the remote holder R's release (remote-release-skips-guard). The local release takes the guard so that no change of the lock bypasses it; the real-code test 'takes the guard to release' (audit-toolchain.test.ts) pins it with a peer that is told it is on another computer.
mutations.search: /\ pc[p] = "cs" /\ Goto(p, IF GuardedRel THEN "rl_guard" ELSE "rel_mine")

mutations.name: acquire-without-peek
mutations.why: Plain acquire that takes the guard even when the lock is there: two waiters polling a lock whose holder died keep the guard taken, and every takeover finds it busy (a livelock).

mutations.name: stale-condemns-a-live-local-holder
mutations.why: Staleness applied to a holder on this computer too (the code before the second fix): a laptop asleep past staleMs loses its lock to a takeover while its work is still running.

mutations.name: plain-acquire-skips-guard-nofailure
mutations.why: The same mutation seen through NoFailure: a process asleep between mkdir and its owner write has its half-made folder removed by a takeover, and its owner write then fails with ENOENT.
mutations.search: /\ gown' = p /\ UNCHANGED gstalled /\ ctx' = [ctx EXCEPT ![p] = "ac"] /\ Goto(p, "acq_mkdir")

mutations.name: no-guard-recheck
mutations.why: A holder that stalled past the guard's 30 s (its guard reclaimed, another holder working under it, the lock replaced) acts on the lock it judged before the stall: it deletes the lock the other holder made.

mutations.name: recheck-ignores-the-token
mutations.why: A check that only asks 'was the guard taken a moment ago' passes for a holder whose guard was reclaimed and taken again by another process: its fresh guard looks like the holder's own.

mutations.name: recheck-ignores-the-stall
mutations.why: A check that only compares the token passes for a holder that stalled but whose guard nobody reclaimed yet.
mutations.equivalent: A stalled holder whose guard is still its own is the only process under the guard: nothing else can change the lock before it acts. The time bound (GUARD_BUDGET_MS) narrows the window in which a reclaim can land between the check and the call; the model has no clock for that window and keeps it as the assumption stated in SCOPE.md (MC_stall_gap.cfg shows what the window costs).

mutations.name: stale-guard-reclaimed-by-name
mutations.why: A stale guard removed by its name after it was judged: the holder finished and another process made a new guard under that name in between, and the reclaimer removes that live guard (two processes inside the guard).

mutations.name: no-fairness
mutations.why: Without fairness a waiter may stop forever; Termination must catch that.
